preconditions: The Phase 5 fixture protocols, scenario catalog, and normalization policy are validated as disposable and non-public.
The exact Phase 4 runtime, browser toolchain, Phoenix endpoint, and governed profile artifacts remain pinned.
The local behavior AVM and DOM fixture adapter match the generated deployment manifest.
steps: Run the nested-state, field, timer/message, DOM-update, accessibility-observation, failure, restart, and disposal scenarios through the real browser runtime.
Repeat the complete scenario in an independent browser context and compare normalized semantic checkpoint hashes.
Exercise malformed, oversized, stale, duplicate, missing-target, crash, post-disposal, and partial-batch cases.
Capture governed network paths, runtime/bridge/DOM ownership, preliminary timings, accessibility observations, and terminal cleanup.
expected_results: Both runs produce the same 29-checkpoint semantic trace and no local-behavior network request after readiness.
Keyed state, normalized form input, local validation, timers, messages, and renderer-owned DOM updates preserve generation and identity.
All declared negative cases fail closed, including atomic rollback of a partial DOM batch.
Explicit stop and generation replacement converge runtime, bridge, lifecycle, listener, and root ownership to zero.
prohibited_results: Browser or DOM objects cross into Elixir fixture state, or the disposable protocols become public BlazeX contracts.
A local interaction requires a server round trip or creates an undeclared network request.
A stale generation mutates current state, a failed DOM batch partially commits, or disposal leaves owned work.
The single-browser observation is represented as browser support, accessibility compliance, or a passed performance budget.
